evidence.content:
Player Dashboard Overview
The dashboard gives you quick access to your teams, upcoming matches, completed
matches, team standings, and your play history. If you are a member of multiple teams,
select the correct team under My Team in the sidebar to update the view.
Dashboard Highlights:
• Top Navigation: At the very top right of the Player Dashboard, you can access the
Player User Guide, email the league, or click the button next to your name to update
your profile, change your password, adjust appearance settings, or view your club
membership.
• Sidebar Options: Use the sidebar menu to switch between teams if you belong to
more than one, view your personal Play History, and check the Division Schedule
or Standings. Select League Documents to view all available files for your league.
• Team Information: The main dashboard gives you immediate access to your next
match, including buttons for match details and posted lineups. You can monitor your
team's rank, record, and your personal Season DUPR rating, as well as review
upcoming schedules and recent results.
• In the My Team section, click on any captain to send them an email, or select View
Team to see the complete player roster with DUPR ratings and individual records.
Player Dashboard Main Screen (Desktop view)

document.title: LWRPC-Players Guide to the LMS

evidence.content:
Viewing My Teams Information
If you are on multiple teams, you can easily switch between them. Go to the sidebar, select
My Team, and choose the team you want to see.
The team page displays:
• Next Match: Shows at the top with quick links to Match Details and Match Lineup
(if available).
• Team Performance: Displays your team's current record, rank and your personal
season DUPR rating.
• Schedules & Results: Lists of upcoming matches and recent match results.
• Team Roster: Shows your full roster. Tap or click any captain's card to email them
directly.
• League Documents: Access all current league files via the sidebar option.
For more details, see the sections below on Team Roster, Division Standings, and Team
Matches.

document.title: LWRPC-Players Guide to the LMS

evidence.content:
Viewing Your Play History
My Play History lets a player review their recorded league match results and performance
across the league.
Use the Play History Scope list to choose which results to view:
• All Seasons/All Teams
• A specific season, league, division, or team
The page updates immediately to show only results within the selected scope.
At the top, summary cards show:
• Games Played — the number of recorded match-line results in the selected scope.
• Wins — recorded individual line wins.
• Losses — recorded individual line losses.
• Other Category - Tracks non-counting personal games, such as forfeits and
Picklebreaker matches. Scores Pending — matches whose scores have not yet been
entered and posted.
Below the summary, each match shows the match date, teams, home/away status, season,
league, division, lines played, and available game scores. A match that still needs scoring is
clearly labeled Scores Not Entered rather than being shown as an unclear “Other” result.
Select More Player Details in the header to open a separate, scrollable details window. It
provides five additional groups of scope-specific information:
• Matches: wins, losses, and match win percentage.
• Games: individual game wins, losses, and game win percentage.
• Points: points earned, points against, and point differential percentage.
• Ratings: average recorded partner and opponent ratings, plus adjusted and overall
performance estimates.
• Last 5 Matchups: the player’s five most recent results, marked with W or L.
The details window is designed for mobile as well as desktop and can be closed without
changing the selected History Scope.
• Mobile Shortcut: Tap the Play History icon in the bottom navigation bar.

evidence.heading: CAPTAIN/CO-CAPTAIN REQUIREMENTS
evidence.content:
CAPTAIN/CO-CAPTAIN REQUIREMENTS
Each League team must have a designated Captain. A Captain may also serve as Co-Captain on
another team and may captain a team in the opposite gender category. However, a person may not
captain more than one team within the same gender category. There can be up to two Co-Captains.
Community Team Captains and Co-Captains have “Captain” access to the League Management
System (LMS) at league.lwrpickleballclub.com to manage teams, rosters, schedules, scores, and
overall league information. (For general club details, visit the main website at lwrpickleballclub.com).
Captains are responsible for their team roster, each match date setup including reserving all home
courts, recording/validating scores and general team management. Club League Management is
available at any time for help with any questions or concerns. See last page for contact information.
Team Home Court Expectations: All teams registering for league play are expected to host their share
of scheduled home matches by providing adequate court availability, resulting in a balanced home-
and-away schedule whenever possible. If a team cannot reserve enough courts for all its assigned
home match dates, additional matches may be scheduled as away games. Teams that are unable to
provide any courts due to limitations within their community or facility will play all their scheduled
matches as away games.
All league players also have access to the LMS through their personal Player Dashboard, where they
can view their assigned teams, upcoming and completed matches, team rosters, and standings. It also
features a full personal play history and quick-click shortcuts to email team captains. Captains can
also switch to the Player Dashboard to see their personal league information.

evidence.content:
CREATE/UPDATE TEAM ROSTER
o Enter or update your player team roster prior to the commencement of each season. Use the
Manage Roster option to add or remove players.
 All players must be active Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club members before playing. To
join, they can visit: https://lwrpickleballclub.com/signup.
 All DUPR League players must have a free DUPR ID which can be created at
https://www.dupr.com.
 All players must join the Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club DUPR club (free and
separate from the LWR PC membership) so we can accurately sync player ratings.
Captains should share this link with all players: https://tinyurl.com/LWRPC-DUPRCLUB.
o Roster Requirements & Substitutes: Teams must roster enough players and substitutes (who
are not already on another team) to field a full lineup weekly. For example, if your match
requires 6 players, an 8–10 player roster is recommended. Additional substitutes may be drawn
from other teams in the same community, provided they meet the DUPR division rating
requirements. For complete details, see the Player Requirements and DUPR Rating/Divisions
sections in the DUPR League Mission and Rules.
o Captain Roster Control: Captains are responsible for building their own rosters and may add
or delete players throughout the season as needed provided the player is a current, valid
member of the LWR PC, has a DUPR ID and is eligible for that division.
o Player DUPR Ratings: Season DUPR ratings are updated in the LMS before the season starts
and remain visible to captains all season. For players added midseason, their rating is based on
the date the league's season ratings were originally recorded.

evidence.heading: TEAM/GAME RULES
evidence.content:
5. TEAM/GAME RULES
5.1. Team Home Court Expectations: All teams registering for league play are expected to
host their share of scheduled home matches by providing adequate court availability,
resulting in a balanced home-and-away schedule whenever possible. If a team cannot
reserve enough courts for all its assigned home match dates, additional matches may be
scheduled as away games. Teams that are unable to provide any courts due to limitations
within their community or facility will play all their scheduled matches as away games.
5.2. Governing Rules & Equipment Standards: All matches are governed by USA Pickleball
Rules (https://usapickleball.org/) and equipment standards including USA Pickleball
approved equipment. In the event of a conflict, specific Lakewood Ranch Pickleball Club
(LWR PC) rules shall take precedence over the corresponding USA Pickleball rules and
regulations.
5.3. Point Scoring Methods: Unless otherwise specifically stated, all games shall use
Standard Scoring as defined by the current USA Pickleball (USAP) Rules. Rally Scoring

shall be used only when a particular game or match format expressly identifies Rally
Scoring as the required scoring method.
5.4. Unauthorized Equipment Penalty: Games played with unauthorized paddles or
equipment will be forfeited, not recorded, and not posted to DUPR if discovered by
players/captains during or after play.
5.5. Match Setup and Roster Exchange: Home and visiting Captains must submit their
upcoming match rosters through the League Management System (LMS) using the Match
Setup button no later than three (3) days prior to the scheduled match. It is strongly
recommended that the Home Team submit its lineup first. Automated reminder emails
will be sent to all Captains. Any lineup or roster changes made after the initial submission
must be entered through Match Setup, which will automatically notify the opposing
Captain(s) of the change. Teams that have not completed Match Setup will not be able to
print a completed Match Score Sheet. Repeated failure to complete Match Setup within
the required timeframe may result in forfeiture of the current or future matches, at the
discretion of League Management.
5.6. Roster Requirements & Retroactive Additions: All active players must appear on the
team’s roster in the LMS prior to match play. Retroactive additions are permitted without
penalty only if the player is a valid LWR PC member with an eligible DUPR account and
rating. Failure to meet these requirements will result in a match forfeit, and the match will
not be posted to DUPR.
5.7. DUPR Submission & Eligibility: All qualifying games will be automatically entered into
the DUPR rating system. Games that are forfeited, incomplete, or deemed ineligible will
not be recorded in DUPR (unless otherwise specified by a rule). Individuals/Players are

evidence.content:

forfeiture of the games.
5.13. Makeup Game Deadline: All makeup games must be played at least one week before the
playoƯs/championship date.
5.14. Weather Interruptions & Mid-Match Stoppages: If weather or other factors interrupt
play after a match has started, the following rules apply based on progress:
5.14.1. Less than half of the games completed: Remaining games should be
rescheduled. Only fully completed games will count toward final scores;
unfinished or unplayed games will not be recorded.
5.14.2. At least half of the games are completed: Completed results will stand. Any
remaining unplayed games may be either rescheduled or canceled as agreed upon
by both Captains (rescheduling is the preferred option).
5.14.3. Roster Continuity: When a game is rescheduled, the players originally assigned to
it must participate and maintain their original positions/line assignments.
5.15. End of Season PlayoƯs/Championship Day (All Leagues)
5.15.1. Teams starting the season with fewer scheduled games than others in their
Division/Pool will receive compensatory points at the end of the season. These
points will be calculated based on the team’s average points earned per match
date, rounded to the nearest whole number (0.5 and above rounds up; 0.4 and
below rounds down).
5.15.2. PlayoƯs feature the top 4 teams per Division based on the LMS points; ties are
settled by Line/Game Win %, then point diƯerential, and finally a coin flip. For
divisions with 2 pools, the top 2 teams from each pool advance to playoƯs.
5.15.3. PlayoƯs will take place the week following the last regular season games, with all
games played at one location.

evidence.heading: Scheduling

potential Picklebreaker™ to 15. Teams will switch ends before Game 2. If a
third game is required, teams will switch ends during Game 3 when the first
team reaches six (6) points. Visitors choose serve, receive, side, or defer in
game 1 and 3. Each team receives one one-minute timeout/game.

the Picklebreaker™ format with the winning team collecting 1 additional point.
If there isn’t a tie, the leading team collects a 1-point bonus.

following completion of all preceding rounds. The Picklebreaker™ features the

document.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules

evidence.content:
6.2. Saturday DUPR League
The Saturday DUPR League is designed for players who prefer weekend competition or are
unable to participate during the week. This coed league features community-based teams
made up of both men and women, competing every other Saturday in a unique format that
includes men's doubles, women's doubles, mixed doubles and the exciting mixed doubles
Picklebreaker to determine tied matches. Teams are grouped into divisions based on
combined DUPR ratings, creating competitive and enjoyable matches while fostering
camaraderie and community spirit throughout the Lakewood Ranch area.

document.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules

evidence.heading: Scheduling
evidence.content:
6.2.1. Scheduling: Games are typically scheduled for every other Saturday at noon.
6.2.2. Roster & Courts: 12 players—6 men and 6 women—divided into six teams: 3 men’s
doubles teams and 3 women’s doubles teams. Mixed teams may be formed from
the gender doubles players or can be from additional players who participate only in
the mixed round. Requires 4 courts.

document.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules

evidence.heading: Match Day Format
evidence.content:
6.2.3. Match Day Format: (See table below)
6.2.3.1. All Games: Games to 15 using Rally Scoring* (win by 1). 1 point per win. Two
one-minute timeouts per team/game but no timeouts in Picklebreaker. Teams
switch ends when the first team reaches 8 points. Visitors choose serve,
receive, side, or defer in games 1 and 3 and all mixed games.
6.2.3.2. Men's Round Robin: 3 Men’s teams play Round Robin (from low to high,
Teams 1 to 3). Each player will play 3 games. 9 points possible.
6.2.3.3. Women's Round Robin: 3 Women’s teams play Round Robin (from low to
high, Teams 4 to 6). Each player will play 3 games. 9 points possible.
6.2.3.4. Mixed Round: Create 6 Mixed teams (from low to high, Teams 7 to 12). Each
player will play 1 mixed game. 6 points possible.
6.2.3.5. Picklebreaker™ Game (Only played if tie at the end of all previous rounds -
12-12): Features all the mixed teams that played in the Mixed rounds. This will

be one game to 25 win by 2 using Rally Scoring. The winning team collects 3
additional points. (If there isn’t a tie, the leading team collects a 3-point
bonus.) Note: Picklebreaker matches will not be recorded in DUPR and do not
reflect on individual’s W/L record.
Teams are numbered 1–3 for Men’s Doubles, 4–6 for Women’s Doubles, and 7–12 for Mixed
Doubles. These team numbers correspond directly to the Match Score Sheet printed from the system.
We highly recommend assigning higher team numbers to teams with higher combined skill levels and

The schedule uses two courts for men’s teams and two courts for women’s teams. After the first four
gender-doubles rounds, Men’s Team 3 and Women’s Team 6 play while Mixed Teams 7 and 8 begin.
Round 6 includes the remaining mixed teams. If the match is tied 12-12 after all gender and mixed
doubles, the Picklebreaker is played on two courts using the same mixed teams in the captains’
designated order.

to determine the winner of the 3 bonus points. If there is no tie, the leading team
automatically receives the 3-point bonus.

evidence.content:
6.3. PrimeTime DUPR League
The PrimeTime DUPR League is exclusively for players age 65 and older who want
competitive play against others in the same age group. Using DUPR's 65+ age-based rating
system, the league provides a more level playing field by matching players of similar age and
ability. Separate men's and women's divisions compete weekly with two doubles teams

Rally Scoring Rules
We follow standard USA Pickleball rally scoring option rules (Section 14.A) with the
following clarifications/modifications:
• Service Positioning: After a side out, the first serve is determined by the team's
score: the player on the right (baseline facing the net) serves if the score is even, and
the player on the left serves if the score is odd.
• Switching Sides: Players only switch sides after winning a point on their own serve.
The same player continues serving from the new side.
• Side Outs & Scoring: If the serving team loses a rally, a side out occurs; the
opposing team earns a point and takes over the serve.
• Game Points: A team can win a point regardless of whether they are serving or
receiving except for the winning point (see next item).
• Scoring Freeze and Match Point: To keep the game competitive through the final
point, a scoring freeze shall take eƯect whenever a team reaches one point below
the game-winning score. Once a team reaches the freeze point, it may score the
game-winning point only while serving. For example, in a game played to 25 points,
a team’s score shall initially freeze at 24. The scoring freeze applies only to the team
that has reached the freeze point; the opposing team may continue to score using
normal Rally Scoring until it also reaches the applicable freeze point. A team must
be serving to score the game-winning point.
• Win-by-Two (2) Games: When the game is played using a win-by-two (2) format
and the score becomes tied at or beyond the initial freeze point, neither team can
win by scoring the next point. Therefore, both teams’ scores shall become
unfrozen, and normal Rally Scoring shall resume. Thereafter, a team’s score shall
freeze again whenever it reaches a score at which its next point would win the

evidence.heading: PICKLEBREAKER™ GAME OVERVIEW
evidence.content:
PICKLEBREAKER™ GAME OVERVIEW
The Picklebreaker™ is our league’s tiebreaker format, similar to Major League Pickleball’s (MLP)
Dreambreaker. It is used when a match is tied after the day’s regular games. Unlike the MLP
version, our Picklebreaker uses doubles rather than singles.
Here is how it works:
The Format: The Picklebreaker™ is a doubles game played to either 15 or 25 points, depending
on the league. It always uses Rally Scoring, where every rally/serve earns a point regardless of
which team served. Refer to the league-specific rules for Rally Scoring, total points, and win-by
requirements.
The Rotations: Each team’s designated doubles pairs shall enter the game in the order
established by their captain prior to the start of play. Both doubles pairs currently on the
court shall remain in play until the combined game score reaches the next rotation
threshold, at which time both pairs shall rotate out and the next designated doubles pair from
each team shall enter.
For games played to 15 points, two (2) designated doubles pairs from each team shall
participate in the rotation, with substitutions occurring after every four (4) combined points
scored.
For games played to 25 points, six (6) designated doubles pairs from each team shall
participate in the rotation, with substitutions occurring after every four (4) combined points
scored.
Each newly substituted doubles pair shall resume play at the existing score and remain on the
court until the next applicable four (4) combined-point rotation threshold is reached.
If the game continues beyond the initial rotation of all designated doubles pairs, the
rotation shall return to the doubles pairs that began the game and continue in the same

document.title: LWR Pickleball Club DUPR League Rules

evidence.heading: PICKLEBREAKER™ GAME OVERVIEW
evidence.content:
established order. The rotation process shall continue, as necessary, until the game is
completed and a winner is determined in accordance with the applicable scoring rules.
The Lineups: Captains determine the lineup order, making strategy an important part of the
game. They must decide whether to start with their strongest team or save that team for the
finish. The changing matchups shift the game’s momentum, while teammates cheering adds
energy and excitement that can help push a team toward victory.
With short doubles sequences and teams ready to rotate in quickly, the Picklebreaker creates a
tense, exciting finish to a full day of pickleball.

evidence.content:
Quick Start Guide
As a Captain, use the League Management System to view schedules, manage rosters, see
division standings, check match details, and find other Captains' contact info. From the
upcoming match details screens, you can set your lineup, print score sheets, and enter or
validate match scores. If you manage multiple teams, a tab for each team will appear in your
My Teams section.
Mobile Device Usage
The system is fully optimized for desktop computers, tablets, and mobile devices. Please
note that most of the screenshots and instructions in this guide are based on the desktop
version. Layouts, menus, and navigation will automatically adapt to your screen size, so
display and functionality may differ slightly when using a mobile device.

evidence.content:
Captain Dashboard Overview
Use the dashboard to overall manage your team(s), keep on top of all upcoming and prior
matches, manage rosters, view standings, and handle score tasks. If you captain multiple
teams, select the correct team under My Team in the sidebar to update the view.
Dashboard Highlights:
• Top Navigation: At the very top right of the Captain Dashboard, you can access the
Captain User Guide, email the league, or click the button next to your name to
update your profile, change your password, adjust appearance settings, or view your
club membership.
• Sidebar Options: Click League Documents to view all available files for your
league.
• Quick Links/Captain Toolbar: Access your team list, manage your team and see
your division schedules and division captain contacts.
• Team Information: Your main dashboard gives you quick access to your next
match—complete with quick-action buttons for match setup. You can also monitor
your team's current rank, record, and any pending score entry or validations,
alongside quick-view sections for division standings, upcoming schedules, and
recent match results.

To update your team roster, go to the Captain Tools section on your Captain Dashboard
and click Manage Roster to add, change, or remove players.

Change Captain/Co-Captain next to your team name. This opens an email draft to

Player Eligibility & DUPR Ratings
Click the Add Player button to add a player to your roster.
• Selection: A pop-up window will appear with your home community preselected.
Use the drop-down menu to view available players, along with their eligibility status
and DUPR ratings.
• Missing DUPR Info: If a player is missing a DUPR ID or Season Rating, select the
player and click Add Player to Team. League Management will automatically be
notified to review the issue and update you on their status.

display an on-screen message explaining the specific reason why.
Add Player Pop-up Window

document.title: LWRPC-Captains Guide to the LMS

evidence.content:
Match Setup Process
Captains must assign player pairings and save their lineups before the match date. To
ensure fair play, the system automatically checks entries against division ranges, team
totals, and Season DUPR ratings, displaying an on-screen warning if a combination is
ineligible. It is highly recommended that the Home Team enter their lineup first. Lineups
can be changed prior to match day with all changes automatically emailed to opposing
captains.
• In Match Setup, roster choices are filtered against the division’s configured rating
type: Season DUPR, or Age-based/PrimeTime (season_primetime_rating). Players
with no valid rating or outside the division minimum/maximum cannot be selected.
It also checks the two-player combined rating cap.
• Before saving, it refreshes the season ratings and validates again. The save API
repeats that validation server-side, including roster membership, individual rating
range, duplicates, and team-rating maximum.
The rating source is selected by the division’s rating_type: standard divisions use Season
DUPR; PrimeTime/Age-based divisions use the Season PrimeTime rating.
The Match Setup button will show as red if your setup is incomplete, and blue once it is
completed. When both teams have completed their setup, the Match Score Sheet button
will turn green, allowing you to print a complete match score sheet.
Saving a lineup (press the Save Match Setup button) automatically notifies the opposing
captain of the update. From this screen, you can also use the Email Players button to notify
all selected players or the entire team.
For any questions regarding player ratings or eligibility, contact
info@lwrpickleballclub.com.

The Weekday DUPR League is designed for players who have the flexibility to play during

organized using DUPR team rating ranges to promote balanced competition while providing
players with regular opportunities to improve their skills, build friendships, and enjoy the
excitement of representing their community.
